fields.lead: Squilla is an open-source, Go-based content management system built around one idea: an AI agent should be able to build, populate, and operate an entire website with zero human intervention. Every operation is exposed as an MCP tool. Every feature lives in a sovereign gRPC extension. The kernel stays small, the system stays fast.
fields.headline: The CMS where AI does the work.

fields.p1_body: ~50 MCP tools across 15 domains. An agent can register custom node types, seed content, activate themes, manage extensions, render previews — all through structured calls. No filesystem access required.
fields.p2_body: The core is a minimal kernel: nodes, rendering, auth, CoreAPI. Everything feature-specific (media, email, forms, SEO) is a gRPC plugin extension that owns its full stack — database tables, business logic, admin UI, migrations.
fields.p2_code:
$ ls extensions/
forms/        media/
email/        sitemap/
fields.p3_body: Atomic operations for hot-swapped config maps. Pre-resolved layouts. JSONB + GIN indexes. PostgreSQL connection pooling. No N+1 queries. The CMS gets out of the way.

fields.lead: Squilla's architecture is borrowed from operating systems: the kernel does the minimum required to be a CMS, and everything else is a sovereign extension. Disable an extension and there is no dead code in core. Add a new extension and it brings its own database tables, HTTP routes, admin UI pages, scripts, and migrations.
fields.rule: If disabling an extension would leave dead code in core, that code belongs in the extension, not the core.

fields.lead: A Squilla theme is a self-contained package: layouts, partials, content blocks, assets, Tengo scripts that seed content on activation. Activating a theme runs its theme.tengo script — registering node types, taxonomies, and seeding pages — with zero server restart.

rows.value: Atomic content units. Self-contained, schema-defined, render with their own field data only.

fields.callout: Activate a theme. The CMS reorganizes itself around it. No restart.
fields.heading:
Themes are
sovereign too.
fields.code_body:
core    := import("core/cms")
nodes   := import("core/nodes")
events  := import("core/events")

// register the recipe node type
nodes.register_type({
  slug: "recipe",
  fields: [
    {name: "hero_image",   type: "media"},
    {name: "prep_minutes", type: "int"},
    {name: "servings",     type: "int"},
    {name: "ingredients",  type: "repeater"},
    {name: "instructions", type: "richtext"},
  ]
})

// seed a starter recipe
core.node_create({
  type:  "recipe",
  title: "Caramelized scallops",
  fields: { prep_minutes: 18, servings: 2 }
})

events.emit("theme.seeded", { theme: "hello-vietnam" })

bullets.text: Atomic configuration maps — hot-swapped without locks
Pre-resolved layout trees — no template lookup at request time
JSONB + GIN indexes for content — sub-millisecond field queries
PostgreSQL connection pooling — saturated under load
No N+1 queries — eager-loaded relations across all read paths
Sub-50ms TTFB target on public pages, measured in CI
